record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.original_question: Does there exist an oracle A such that BQP^A is not contained in IP^A, where IP is the class of languages that admit classical interactive proofs and oracle-relative behavior may differ from the unrelativized equality IP=PSPACE?

evidence.quote: Let IP be the class of languages that admit classical interactive proofs. In the unrelativized world, IP = PSPACE [45], but it’s well-known that the situation relative to oracles can be dramatically different [32]. Thus we ask:
Problem 7 Does there exist an oracle A such that BQPA̸⊂ IPA?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let IP denote the complexity class of languages admitting a classical interactive proof system: a language L is in IP if there is a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier V and a (computationally unbounded) prover P such that, on every input x ∈ L, V interacting with P accepts with probability at least 2/3, while on every x ∉ L and for every prover P*, V interacting with P* accepts with probability at most 1/3. Let BQP denote the class of languages decided with bounded error by polynomial-time quantum Turing machines. For any oracle A, let BQP^A and IP^A be the corresponding classes when the verifier (and, in the case of BQP^A, the polynomial-time quantum machine; in the case of IP^A, both the prover and the verifier) have query access to A.

Does there exist an oracle A such that BQP^A ⊄ IP^A?
artifact.category_tag: Quantum query complexity and oracle separations
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding an oracle A with BQP^A ⊄ IP^A appears to still be open. Although Raz and Tal (2019/2022) established an oracle separation BQP^A ⊄ PH^A, IP is much larger than PH relative to oracles, and no oracle separating BQP from IP is reported in the literature. Recent related work has instead shown that BQP is contained in MIP relative to all classical oracles, leaving the BQP vs. IP relativized question unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Oracle Separation of BQP and PH (Raz–Tal)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an oracle A with BQP^A not in PH^A.
status_evidence.claim: Best known related separation is BQP vs PH, not BQP vs IP.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity (problem list)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open problem whether there exists an oracle A with BQP^A ⊄ IP^A.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open in a recent survey of quantum query complexity open problems.
